questions.question: What is a scientific claim?
choices: A raw measurement with no interpretation
A statement proposed as an answer or explanation
An instrument's unit symbol
A bibliography entry only

questions.question: What counts as empirical evidence?
choices: The popularity of an idea alone
An author's confidence alone
A preferred outcome
Relevant observations or measurements

questions.question: What is reasoning in a claim-evidence-reasoning explanation?
choices: The connection between evidence and claim using scientific principles
A repetition of the title
A list of equipment only
An unsupported opinion

questions.question: What is a counterargument?
choices: A requirement to reject all evidence
A second copy of the same conclusion
An alternative explanation or challenge to a claim
A measurement unit

questions.question: What is a limitation of evidence?
choices: Proof that every result is false
A reason never to collect more data
An explanation unrelated to methods
A factor restricting what the evidence can support

questions.question: What is anecdotal evidence?
choices: A carefully sampled population measurement in every case
A complete controlled experiment by definition
An individual account that may not represent a broader pattern
A mathematical proof

questions.question: What is confirmation bias?
choices: Favoring information that supports an existing belief
Recording data before forming a conclusion
Considering contradictory results fairly
Reporting uncertainty explicitly

questions.question: Why should evidence be relevant to the specific claim?
choices: Any number supports every scientific claim
A true observation may still fail to address the proposed explanation
Relevance depends only on source popularity
Measurements always have identical meanings

questions.question: Why can a large sample help support a population-level conclusion?
choices: It automatically removes every sampling bias
It guarantees causation
It makes measurement quality irrelevant
It can reduce random sampling variation when collected appropriately

questions.question: Why should alternative explanations be considered?
choices: Science requires accepting all explanations equally
More than one process may fit the same observations
Alternatives replace the need for data
A claim cannot be revised once written

questions.question: Why is uncertainty part of a strong scientific argument?
choices: It proves that no knowledge is possible
It means the evidence must be hidden
It makes the strength and limits of the inference clearer
It requires choosing the least likely conclusion

questions.question: Why should a scientific argument separate observation from interpretation?
choices: Readers need to identify what was measured and what was inferred
Interpretations are always direct measurements
Observations cannot be communicated
Only personal opinions belong in conclusions

questions.question: Why is a scientist's authority alone insufficient evidence?
choices: The claim still requires methods and data that can be evaluated
Qualified scientists never produce useful work
Credentials determine every experimental result
Scientific claims are settled by voting

questions.question: How should conflicting reliable evidence be handled?
choices: Choose only the preferred result
Assume the later result must be false
Compare methods, conditions, and possible explanations for the difference
Combine unrelated values without examining context

questions.question: What strengthens an argument about a causal effect?
choices: A graph with two trending variables alone
Evidence that addresses competing explanations and isolates the proposed cause
A single testimonial alone
A conclusion chosen before collecting observations

questions.question: A claim says a fertilizer improves growth. The evidence is only the fertilizer's color. What is the main weakness?
choices: The claim must be true because color is observable
Any observation automatically measures growth
A fertilizer's appearance determines its effect on all plants
The evidence does not measure the claimed growth effect

questions.question: One plant grows better after treatment, but no comparison plants are measured. What conclusion is most appropriate?
choices: The treatment is proven effective for all plants
The result proves that sunlight has no effect
The observation alone does not isolate the treatment's effect
Further measurements cannot improve the evidence

questions.question: Two materials are compared in repeated fair tests; one consistently transfers less heat. Which claim is best supported?
choices: Under tested conditions, it is the better thermal insulator
It is the strongest material under every load
It never transfers any energy
It is better for every possible engineering purpose

questions.question: A report concludes that every bird species benefits from one feeding method after testing one species. What is the problem?
choices: A study cannot measure feeding
One bird species represents every species perfectly
The conclusion needs no conditions
The conclusion extends beyond the sampled evidence

questions.question: New reliable results contradict a previous explanation. Which response best reflects argument from evidence?
choices: Exclude all new results automatically
Reassess the explanation and the new results together
Keep the explanation because it was published first
Treat disagreement as proof that no testing is useful
